original_uses.context:
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) scales outcome
supervision through executable validation
\citep{shao2024deepseekmath,guo2025deepseekr1}. Yet a conventional verifier
records only correctness: repeated copies and different successful outputs
receive the same scalar reward. A policy can therefore become more accurate as
its support over verified output modes contracts
\citep{liu2025understanding,cui2025entropy,dang2025diversity}. This limitation
weakens repeated sampling, best-of-$K$, and verifier-guided selection: once one
output dominates training, additional samples reproduce the familiar rather
than extend the set available to a selector
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime,cobbe2021training,lightman2023lets}.
Figure~\ref{fig:story} exhibits this failure on one prompt;
Appendix Figure~\ref{fig:baseline-precheck} shows it is systematic. Eight passes of
unmodified Dr.GRPO or GRPO remove $99\%$ and $98\%$ of the base model's
verified breadth beyond its first correct mode at Qwen2.5-0.5B, and
$42$--$72\%$ of it at the two larger scales.
In an idealized model, our analysis shows that additional parameters can
preserve more sampled alternatives at matched accuracy when they strengthen
updates shared across correct outputs
(Appendix~\ref{app:theory-size}, Theorem~\ref{thm:shared-correctness});
size alone provides no guarantee.

\noindent\textbf{Verifiable learning and output support.}
Repeated sampling and verifier-guided selection depend on proposal support
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime}, yet RLHF, fine-tuning, and RLVR can
narrow that support
\citep{kirk2024understanding,dang2025diversity,cui2025entropy,yue2025rlvrlimit}.
Semantic clustering typically infers when generations express the same answer
\citep{farquhar2024detecting}. \mb{} instead lets accepting execution define
the equivalence relation, yielding an exact behavioral key.

\section{Correct answers can conceal the loss of alternatives}
\label{sec:introduction}\label{sec:collapse}
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains from executable
correctness feedback \citep{shao2024deepseekmath,guo2025deepseekr1}, rewarding
familiar and new correct solutions alike. In mathematical search, losing
alternatives limits what repeated sampling can supply to a verifier
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime}. Figure~\ref{fig:story} shows this
failure: correctness rises while sampled alternatives disappear.

\noindent\textbf{Verifiable learning and output support.}
Repeated sampling and verifier-guided selection depend on proposal support
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime}, yet RLHF, fine-tuning, and RLVR can
narrow that support
\citep{kirk2024understanding,dang2025diversity,cui2025entropy,yue2025rlvrlimit}.
Semantic clustering typically infers when generations express the same answer
\citep{farquhar2024detecting}. \mb{} instead lets accepting execution define
the equivalence relation, yielding an exact behavioral key.

correctness feedback \citep{guo2025deepseekr1}. Reasoning RL can reduce policy
entropy and output diversity \citep{cui2025entropy,dang2025diversity}.
A correctness-only reward treats repeated and distinct successes alike; we
show that accuracy can rise while verified-mode support contracts.
Repeated sampling supplies proposals for verifier-guided selection
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime,cobbe2021training,lightman2023lets}.
Concentration leaves fewer verified alternatives, without necessarily reducing
pass@$K$ at fixed per-sample correctness.
Figure~\ref{fig:story} exhibits this failure on one prompt;
Appendix Figure~\ref{fig:baseline-precheck} shows it is systematic. Eight passes of
unmodified Dr.GRPO or GRPO remove $99\%$ and $98\%$ of the base model's
verified breadth beyond its first correct mode at Qwen2.5-0.5B, and
$42$--$72\%$ of it at the two larger scales.
In an idealized model, our analysis shows that additional parameters can
preserve more sampled alternatives at matched accuracy when they strengthen
updates shared across correct outputs
(Appendix~\ref{app:theory-size}, Theorem~\ref{thm:shared-correctness});
size alone provides no guarantee.

\noindent\textbf{Verifiable learning and output support.}
Sampling-based selection depends on the proposal distribution
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime}. Prior work measures reduced output
diversity under RLHF or reasoning RL \citep{kirk2024understanding,dang2025diversity},
declining policy entropy \citep{cui2025entropy}, and reduced high-budget problem
coverage for tested RLVR models \citep{yue2025rlvrlimit}. These metrics differ from
within-prompt execution-key breadth. Semantic clustering infers answer
equivalence \citep{farquhar2024detecting}; \mb{} defines keys by accepting execution.

\item \textbf{ReplayMaxRL explores and preserves.} MaxRL directs fresh-rollout
  learning toward success across sampling budgets \citep{tajwar2026maxrl};
  key-balanced verified replay retains one exemplar per discovered mode and
  revisits modes uniformly. A categorical mean-flow calculation connects the
  objectives to standard replicator dynamics: binary MaxRL inherits binary
  GRPO's winner-take-all instability, while an idealized fixed replay bank adds
  a qualitative barrier against exact extinction.

\noindent\textbf{Sampling-aware exploration.}
Outcome bonuses, entropy control, set objectives, distribution matching, and
uniform-correct objectives encourage broader verified-output support
\citep{song2025outcome,chen2025passktraining,li2025divergence,
li2026setpo,li2026distribution,lochab2026ucpo}. MaxRL jointly
optimizes best@\(k\) objectives through the rollout budget, while ArgMaxRL
extends the construction to continuous rewards \citep{tajwar2026maxrl}.
Because our task rewards are binary, the MaxRL method is the exact binary special
case; ReplayMaxRL tests whether explicit mode memory adds support beyond this
sampling-aware fresh-rollout objective.

For a fresh group of $G$ binary rewards $r_{1:G}$, let
$m=\sum_{i=1}^G r_i$. The implemented MaxRL task advantage is
\[
  A_i^{\mathrm{MaxRL}}=
  \begin{cases}
    G r_i/m-1, & m>0,\\
    0, & m=0.
  \end{cases}
\]
When successes are scarce, their weight increases; failures receive $-1$.
All-failure and all-success groups have zero task advantage. This is the
binary special case of ArgMaxRL and optimizes best@\(k\) across sampling
budgets \citep{tajwar2026maxrl}. It is applied only to fresh on-policy rows.

\noindent\textbf{Sampling-aware exploration.}
Outcome bonuses, entropy control, set objectives, distribution matching, and
uniform-correct objectives encourage broader verified-output support
\citep{song2025outcome,chen2025passktraining,li2025divergence,
li2026setpo,li2026distribution,lochab2026ucpo}. MaxRL jointly
optimizes best@\(k\) objectives through the rollout budget, while ArgMaxRL
extends the construction to continuous rewards \citep{tajwar2026maxrl}.
Because our task rewards are binary, the MaxRL method is the exact binary special
case; ReplayMaxRL tests whether explicit mode memory adds support beyond this
sampling-aware fresh-rollout objective.

For a fresh on-policy group of $G$ responses, let $r_i\in\{0,1\}$ be the
verified reward of response $i$ and let $m=\sum_{i=1}^G r_i$ count successes.
The binary MaxRL task advantage is
\[
  A_i^{\mathrm{MaxRL}}=
  \begin{cases}
    G r_i/m-1, & m>0,\\
    0, & m=0.
  \end{cases}
\]
Mixed groups assign failures advantage $-1$ and increase the weight of each
success when successes are scarce. All-correct and all-failure groups have
zero task advantage. This is the binary special case of ArgMaxRL and
optimizes a harmonic mixture of best@\(k\) for $k=1,\ldots,G-1$
\citep{tajwar2026maxrl}. It is applied only to fresh on-policy responses;
replay exemplars enter through the separate verified-likelihood loss.

\section{Correct answers can conceal the loss of alternatives}
\label{sec:introduction}\label{sec:collapse}
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains from executable
correctness feedback \citep{shao2024deepseekmath,guo2025deepseekr1}, rewarding
familiar and new correct solutions alike. In mathematical search, losing
alternatives limits what repeated sampling can supply to a verifier
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime}. Figure~\ref{fig:story} shows this
failure: correctness rises while sampled alternatives disappear.

final_uses.context:
GRPO \citep{shao2024deepseekmath} and Dr.GRPO \citep{liu2025understanding}
center binary rewards within sampled groups, giving correct responses equal
task credit regardless of execution key. Common correct modes therefore appear
in more updates; absent modes supply no direct signal.

MaxRL trains policy $\pi_\theta$ for success within $k$ samples across sampling
budgets \citep{tajwar2026maxrl}. Each training prompt $x$ keeps one
policy-generated exemplar $e_c$ per admitted key in bank $\mathcal B_x$.
With $|e_c|$ its token length, recurrent replay minimizes
\begin{equation}
L_{\mathrm{replay}}(x)=-\frac{1}{|\mathcal B_x|}
\sum_{c\in\mathcal B_x}\frac{\log\pi_\theta(e_c\mid x)}{|e_c|}.
\label{eq:lm-verified-replay}
\end{equation}
Equal averaging of per-token scores makes replay independent of discovery frequency. Replacing MaxRL with Dr.GRPO \citep{liu2025understanding},
which debiases GRPO \citep{shao2024deepseekmath}, yields our ReplayDr.GRPO.
Appendix~\ref{app:algorithm} gives
the full update. Appendix~\ref{app:theory} proves categorical collapse and
replay retention (Theorems~\ref{thm:grpo-collapse} and~\ref{thm:replay-retention}).

GRPO \citep{shao2024deepseekmath} and Dr.GRPO \citep{liu2025understanding}
center binary rewards within sampled groups, giving correct responses equal
task credit regardless of execution key. Common correct modes therefore appear
in more updates; absent modes supply no direct signal.

MaxRL trains policy $\pi_\theta$ for success within $k$ samples across sampling
budgets \citep{tajwar2026maxrl}. Each training prompt $x$ keeps one
policy-generated exemplar $e_c$ per admitted key in bank $\mathcal B_x$.
With $|e_c|$ its token length, recurrent replay minimizes
\begin{equation}
L_{\mathrm{replay}}(x)=-\frac{1}{|\mathcal B_x|}
\sum_{c\in\mathcal B_x}\frac{\log\pi_\theta(e_c\mid x)}{|e_c|}.
\label{eq:lm-verified-replay}
\end{equation}
Equal averaging of per-token scores makes replay independent of discovery frequency. Replacing MaxRL with Dr.GRPO \citep{liu2025understanding},
which debiases GRPO \citep{shao2024deepseekmath}, yields our ReplayDr.GRPO.
Appendix~\ref{app:algorithm} gives
the full update. Appendix~\ref{app:theory} proves categorical collapse and
replay retention (Theorems~\ref{thm:grpo-collapse} and~\ref{thm:replay-retention}).

original_uses.context:
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) scales outcome
supervision through executable validation
\citep{shao2024deepseekmath,guo2025deepseekr1}. Yet a conventional verifier
records only correctness: repeated copies and different successful outputs
receive the same scalar reward. A policy can therefore become more accurate as
its support over verified output modes contracts
\citep{liu2025understanding,cui2025entropy,dang2025diversity}. This limitation
weakens repeated sampling, best-of-$K$, and verifier-guided selection: once one
output dominates training, additional samples reproduce the familiar rather
than extend the set available to a selector
\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime,cobbe2021training,lightman2023lets}.
Figure~\ref{fig:story} exhibits this failure on one prompt;
Appendix Figure~\ref{fig:baseline-precheck} shows it is systematic. Eight passes of
unmodified Dr.GRPO or GRPO remove $99\%$ and $98\%$ of the base model's
verified breadth beyond its first correct mode at Qwen2.5-0.5B, and
$42$--$72\%$ of it at the two larger scales.
In an idealized model, our analysis shows that additional parameters can
preserve more sampled alternatives at matched accuracy when they strengthen
updates shared across correct outputs
(Appendix~\ref{app:theory-size}, Theorem~\ref{thm:shared-correctness});
size alone provides no guarantee.

\citep{brown2024monkeys,snell2024testtime}, yet RLHF, fine-tuning, and RLVR can
narrow that support
\citep{kirk2024understanding,dang2025diversity,cui2025entropy,yue2025rlvrlimit}.
Semantic clustering typically infers when generations express the same answer
\citep{farquhar2024detecting}. \mb{} instead lets accepting execution define
the equivalence relation, yielding an exact behavioral key.

\noindent\textbf{Related work.} Prior work studies diversity collapse
\citep{cui2025entropy,dang2025diversity}, sampling-aware objectives, and success
replay \citep{zhang2025rlep}. Our focus is execution-defined identity for
measuring and retaining verified alternatives. Appendix~\ref{sec:related}
gives the full discussion.

which 74 are source-admissible. Fourteen blocks contain five seeds; Falcon
Countdown contains four (Appendix~\ref{app:source-integrity}). The methods
share replay code and differ in whether its derivative is applied. Subsequent
banks, schedules, and realized workloads depend on each policy. Fully matched
Qwen2.5-0.5B blocks also provide direct alternatives: ordinary GRPO
normalization; UCPO on-policy advantage redistribution
\citep{lochab2026ucpo}; our frequency-weighted RLEP-Dr adaptation
\citep{zhang2025rlep}; memoryless binary MaxRL; and fixed Semantic-MaxEnt.
Figure~\ref{fig:cross-scale-terminal-effects}B compares them with
ReplayDr.GRPO. The semantic estimator is defined only as a comparator in
Appendix~\ref{app:semantic-maxent}.

\noindent\textbf{Replay and persistent memory.}
Experience replay reuses past experience and can mitigate forgetting
\citep{lin1992selfimproving,rolnick2019replay}; RLEP reuses successful
reasoning trajectories \citep{zhang2025rlep}. Our replay component instead stores one exemplar per canonical executed key and
samples uniformly over keys, making equal retention an explicit target rather
than depending on how often each success occurs. Novelty search rewards behavioral novelty
\citep{lehman2011novelty}, while MAP-Elites retains one elite per behavior-descriptor
cell \citep{mouret2015illuminating}. Our replay bank uses the execution key
as the descriptor inside a policy-gradient update.
